ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an impedance Smith chart, with the horizontal dashed line labeled x=0; the lower half is labeled with negative reactance arcs such as x=-0.5 and x=-1, and point P is marked with a black dot in the lower half of the chart, close to the position of x=-1. The problem specifies moving 45° clockwise from P along a constant-resistance circle, therefore this path keeps the same resistance r, that is, the R of the impedance remains unchanged. Reasoning: In an impedance Smith chart, moving clockwise along a constant-resistance circle corresponds to the normalized reactance x increasing, that is, moving from a more negative reactance toward a smaller negative value or toward positive reactance. Since R remains unchanged and X increases, it is equivalent to adding a positive series reactance jΔX to the original impedance Z. Positive reactance is provided by an inductor, and the connection method in which impedances are directly added is series. Therefore, this movement is equivalent to adding an inductor in series to Z.

method.method_draft: First describe the chart: identify P on the impedance Smith chart and note that the specified path stays on a constant-resistance circle, so R is unchanged. Then use the chart orientation: in the impedance chart, moving clockwise along a constant-r circle corresponds to increasing normalized reactance x, moving from more capacitive/negative x toward less negative or positive x. Therefore the operation adds a positive reactance to Z while leaving R unchanged. A positive reactance is an inductor, and because impedances add directly only in series, the equivalent operation is adding an inductance in series with Z.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure as an impedance Smith chart and identify the specified path as a rotation on one constant-r circle. Model the plotted point by normalized impedance z=r+jx with r fixed. Under Γ=(z-1)/(z+1), varying x with r fixed traces the resistance circle; the parameterization shows that increasing x corresponds to clockwise motion on that circle. Since the given motion is clockwise, Δx is positive. Thus the new impedance is Z+jX_add with X_add>0. A positive pure reactance is inductive, and the fact that it adds to Z as an impedance means the element is connected in series. Hence the movement is equivalent to adding a series inductance to Z.
